newsitem.title: USA: Second cold snap seen prolonging U.S. cold temps.
newsitem.headline: Second cold snap seen prolonging U.S. cold temps.

text.p: A second cold surge behind the current Arctic front from Canada is expected to prolong into next week cold Midwest and Northeast temperatures, a reversal of earlier forecasts of milder weather to come, Weather Services Corp said.
Originally, forecasters were calling for a warming trend to kick in on Monday after below-normal temperatures through the weekend for both regions.
But instead of the warmup it now "looks like it's turning colder and then staying below normal for the rest of next week," said Joel Burgio of Weather Services Corp.
For the Midcontinent, Weather Services is forecasting temperatures eight to 15-degrees below normal for the weekend and 5 to 10 degrees below normal on Monday.
The Northeast will see normal to two-degrees below normal temperatures on Sunday, a range expected to linger on Monday and beyond, said Weather Services.
"It's not so much how cold it will be, but that it will be staying cool for longer," said Burgio.
